title: Retrieval-augmented generation
blurb: How language models answer from your documents instead of their memory.
suggestions: How do you know if it's working?
Email me at satnam@example.com with the slides

slides.title: Models forget, documents don't
bullets: LLMs only know their training data
slides.notes: Language models only know what they were trained on, and your documents change constantly. Retrieval-augmented generation fetches the relevant passages at question time so the model answers from current facts.
slides.narration: Language models only know what they saw during training, but your documents change every day. Retrieval-augmented generation bridges that gap.

slides.title: Chunking documents
bullets: Split text into passages of a few hundred tokens
Overlap chunks so ideas aren't cut in half
Keep titles and headings as context
slides.notes: Documents are split into passages of a few hundred tokens, with some overlap so an idea isn't cut in half. Keeping the heading with each chunk gives the model context about where it came from.
slides.narration: First, documents are split into chunks of a few hundred tokens, with a little overlap, and each chunk keeps its heading for context.

slides.title: Embeddings and search
bullets: Nearest vectors are the best matches
slides.notes: Each chunk is turned into a vector that captures its meaning. The question is embedded the same way, and the closest vectors are the passages most likely to answer it.
slides.narration: Each chunk becomes a vector that captures its meaning. Your question becomes a vector too, and the nearest ones are the best matches.

slides.title: Grounded answers
bullets: Top passages go into the prompt
The model cites where facts came from
slides.notes: The best passages are placed in the prompt, and the model is told to answer only from them and cite its sources. If nothing relevant is found, it should say so rather than guess.
slides.narration: The best passages go into the prompt. The model answers from them, cites its sources, and admits when nothing matches.

slides.title: Measuring quality
bullets: Retrieval: did we fetch the right passage?
Faithfulness: does the answer match it?
A small golden question set goes far
slides.notes: You measure two things separately: whether retrieval found the right passage, and whether the answer stays faithful to it. Even fifty hand-written golden questions catch most regressions.
slides.narration: To know it's working, measure retrieval and faithfulness separately. Even a small set of golden questions catches most problems.

slides.title: Going to production
slides.notes: In production you re-index whenever documents change, filter results by the user's permissions before retrieval, and log each question with its sources so you can debug bad answers.
slides.narration: In production, keep the index fresh, respect permissions before retrieval, and log every question with its sources.
